notes: Weaknesses deliberately served by app.py. `match_any` holds lowercase substrings; a scanner finding counts as a detection when its id/name contains one of them and it was observed at `path`. Optional `as_actor` names the session a request needs before the weakness is observable (agent findings only). `must_not_detect` lists endpoints that look suspicious but are sound: a finding matching one of those is a false positive, not a detection.

expected.description: Environment file with app key and database/AWS credentials served publicly
Git repository config exposed, leaking the upstream remote
SQL dump with user table and password hashes downloadable without auth
phpinfo() page disclosing PHP version, paths and module config
Upload directory serves an auto-index of stored files
Unauthenticated admin login page advertising default credentials
No X-Frame-Options / CSP / X-Content-Type-Options on any response
Login failure messages differ for unknown accounts and wrong passwords, so the account list is enumerable
Search parameter q is concatenated into SQL: an unbalanced quote raises a DB syntax error and a -- comment repairs it
Order API checks the session but not object ownership, so any signed-in user reads any order

must_not_detect.description: Directory lookup 500s on absurdly long input but never echoes a SQL error, and quotes are handled correctly. An injection finding here is a false positive.
